chunks: As for that which indicates the second principle, namely that it is characteristic of the Imam to be conclusively established in his infallibility,
is that the reason for which we needed the Imam is the absence of infallibility;
as evidence that if the people were infallible, they would not need an Imam, and if they were devoid of being infallible, they would need him;
so we know at that time that the reason for the need is the absence of infallibility,
as we say regarding the reason for the need of an effect to its cause is its occurrence (huduth),
as evidence that that which is capable of occurrence needs a cause in its occurrence, and that which is not capable of occurrence is independent of the cause,
and we rule by that that every created thing needs a Creator,
so similarly it must be ruled that the need of every one who is not infallible to an Imam is obligatory, or else the reason would be invalidated,
so if the Imam were not infallible, the reason for need would remain in him, and he would need another Imam,
and the discussion regarding his Imam is like the discussion regarding him,
leading to the necessity of infinite Imams or to reaching an infallible one, which is the intended meaning.
And this method we have perfected in our books, so we will not prolong the questioning about it, because the purpose of this book is different, and this much suffices.
ai.seo_question: Why must the Shia Imam be infallible according to the principle of causality?
ai.summary: This passage articulates the Shia theological argument for the Imam's infallibility ('ismah) by positing that human fallibility necessitates a guide, and if that guide were also fallible, it would trigger an infinite regress (tawallud) or require a final infallible authority. Shaykh al-Tusi employs the metaphysical principle of 'huduth' (contingency) to demonstrate that the Imam's role as a perfect exemplar requires him to be free from error, ensuring the continuity of divine guidance. This logical proof underscores the necessity of a single, divinely protected leader to prevent the collapse of religious authority.
